history.summary: Tara Devi Temple sits atop Tarav Parvat at about 1,851 metres, roughly 11-15 km from Shimla town. The temple is about 250 years old and, according to local tradition, the idol of Goddess Tara was brought to this hill by rulers of the Sen dynasty from West Bengal; one source names King Bhupendra Sen as the builder (UNVERIFIED). Tara is worshipped as a protective form of Shakti/Durga; the idol is said to be made of eight elements (ashtadhatu, per local claim — verify). The temple was substantially renovated and reopened to the public on 20 July 2018 (per visitor reports). It is a simple Himachali wood-and-stone hill temple with sloping roofs, known as much for its panoramic Himalayan views and serene forested setting as for its religious importance.

town_description: Shimla is the capital of Himachal Pradesh and was the summer capital of British India, set in the Shivalik Hills at about 2,200 metres. The town centres on the Ridge and Mall Road, with colonial-era landmarks like Christ Church and the Viceregal Lodge, and is linked to Kalka by the UNESCO-listed Kalka-Shimla toy train. It is Himachal's main hill-station tourist hub, famous for Himalayan views, apple country around it, and a cluster of well-known temples.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism — Goddess Tara as a form of Durga)

travel.railway: Shimla Railway Station — about 10-12 km (verify); onward by taxi or bus on the Kalka-Shimla National Highway
travel.road: About 11 km from Shimla Bus Stand via the Kalka-Shimla National Highway; taxis and buses available; a forest trek route also leads to the hilltop

visitor_information.best_time: March to June for pleasant weather and clear views; September to December for a spiritual, sometimes snowy atmosphere; avoid July-August monsoon for slippery trails
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): most sources list 7:00 AM to 6:30 PM daily; one travel site says 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Free entry; langar (free food) on Sunday/Tuesday per visitor reports
